verdict.reasoning: Patient reports cough and runny nose, starting “a bit less than a week ago… maybe five or six days ago.”
Patient: “it's just so continuous… quite dry… it's just all day, it like keeps me up at night as well.”
Patient: “the coughing is giving me a sore throat… just my throat is irritated from coughing. But it's not that bad when I swallow or anything,” indicating irritation without odynophagia.

Patient denies baseline breathlessness: “Day to day when you walk around, you don't feel breathless do you? Patient: I don't feel restless. No,” and also “Any pain in your chest? … Patient: No not, not that either.”

Patient mentions tired/lethargic, chills, possible fever without measuring temperature, and muscle aches: “I've been having like, like shivers… I haven't taken my temperature… My muscle was really hurting… Especially like in my arms, my legs, like just everywhere basically… quite lethargic and weak.”
Patient: “No.They feel OK, actually… Nothing, nothing on the ears.” Doctor confirms: “No pain, no discharge coming from your ears.”

Patient: “I had a little bit of diarrhea… Has that got better now, the diarrhea? Patient: Yeah, yeah. It got better… it stopped.” Also: “No, no nausea. No vomiting… How's your appetite? Patient: Um, I mean it's OK.”
When asked about urine: “Any problems with your waterworks at all?... Patient: Ohh. Uh, no. No no, it's fine.”
Patient: “I have type two diabetes.”
Patient: “And I have quite high blood pressure.”
Patient: “I take Metformin for the diabetes.”
Patient: “And I take Lisinopril for the high blood pressure.”
Doctor: “Any allergies at all, to medications?” Patient: “No. No allergies.”
Patient: “my dad also has type two diabetes.”

Patient: “just, it's just me and my partner.” and “I am a developer… yeah. Work in IT.” Doctor paraphrases: “you work in the IT field.” Partner noted as well: “Is your partner well at the moment? Patient: Yeah he has none of this… fine.”
Doctor: “Do you smoke at all, April?” Patient: “I used to, but I've stopped for about six months now.”
Patient: drinks wine “maybe two or three glasses” on “like, let's say three evenings a week?”
Doctor: “you're not bringing up any mucky, ohh I can hear that, yeah,” indicating audible cough during consultation.

Doctor’s assessment: “I think you're going through a bit of a viral illness… you've had a bit of a cough, bit of a runny nose, feeling quite weak and lethargic.” History includes dry cough, rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias for 5–6 days, with “Day to day… you don't feel breathless” and “Any pain in your chest? … No,” and “diarrhea… got better… then it stopped.” This matches an acute viral URTI description.
Patient has type 2 diabetes and states: “I take Metformin for the diabetes,” consistent with T2DM on metformin.
Patient: “I have quite high blood pressure… I take Lisinopril for the high blood pressure,” consistent with HTN on lisinopril.

Alcohol: Patient drinks wine 2–3 glasses up to 3 nights/week; Doctor: “you're probably just about under the limit… maybe something that you can maybe cut down on… really ideally… cut down completely,” indicating current intake is above ideal for HTN/DM. Ex-smoker with cessation 6 months ago is directly stated.

Doctor: “things you can do… get some nice, good rest. Drink plenty of fluids. Keep yourself well-hydrated. You can take regular Paracetamol.” Also: “maybe take a day or two off work, if you can… maybe think about work early next week.” Safety net: “If you feel like you're still not getting any better in two to three days, it's probably worth coming back… If you are still feeling feverish, um and your cough isn't getting any better, then we may look to give you some antibiotics for your chest… if your cough isn't getting any better, or your breathing is getting worse, I want you to come back and see me sooner.”
The plan to continue metformin is not explicitly discussed; metformin is mentioned only in past medical/medication history, without explicit continuation instructions.
The plan to continue lisinopril is not explicitly stated; lisinopril is listed as a current medication, but no explicit continuation advice is given.

Doctor advises alcohol reduction: “maybe for the first few weeks, why don't you cut down to two glasses a week. And then, one week thereafter… if you are coping OK, then you can maybe try and cut down altogether,” which corresponds to reducing to ≤2 glasses/week then further, considering abstinence.
